messages:
sofia: Starting a quick smoke for Zeta13B onboarding. Converted to int4 with our usual toolchain, ran a basic chat regression and noticed weird embed drift on long context (>2k). Anyone else seeing projective mismatch after quant?
kevin: saw something similar locally. small repro: single-turn answer probabilities diverge after ~1024 tokens. looks like embedding projection stepping, not LM head.
anita: can you paste the quant command? I want to check the quant config (group size / outlier handling).
sofia: here's the conversion command we used:
```
redwood-quantize --model zeta13b --dtype int4 --group 64 --outlier-mode clamp --calib-samples 512
```
sofia: calib metrics looked fine (ppl delta ~0.02) but downstream chat rouge dropped ~3 points on our short-answer eval.
kevin: I dumped the first-layer embed matrix before/after. small but consistent low-rank rotation in columns 64..128. suspect projector/transpose assumption mismatch during conversion.
liam: could be tokenizer allied too — Zeta tokenizer has NFKC normalization enabled by default; tokens with zero-width joiners are splitting differently vs our standard tokenizer shim. kvcache indices could get misaligned.
anita: interesting — I also noticed rotary mismatch when we switched head grouping for int4 kernels. Zeta reports 32 heads but the exported metadata had head_dim=128 and head_count=64 in the metadata layer (oof). Might be a head vs headwise packing bug.
sofia: reproduction log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] model.zeta: tokens=2048, latency=85ms, top1=0.62
[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] model.zeta_quant: tokens=2048, latency=60ms, top1=0.48
```
sofia: note top1 collapses after certain token where kvcache read returns shifted rows.
kevin: can you run `inspect-headmap zeta13b --dump-rotary`? my tool shows per-head rotary scale ~= [1.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.5, ...] for quantized model.
sofia: ran that, got weird fractional angles on half the heads. dump: `rotary_scale: 0.999,0.998,0.512,0.507,0.513,0.999...`
anita: fractional angles + headcount metadata mismatch == high chance of headwise packing bug during export. I think the conversion script misread `num_attention_heads` vs `num_key_value_heads`.
liam: on tokenizer front I cross-checked: original tokenizer returns token ids for the prefix as [101, 523, 3021, 2] while our shim returned [101, 523, 3021, 2, 0] — an extra sentinel. That will shift kvcache offsets by one for affected batches.
kevin: urgent triage checklist: 1) verify tokenizer NFKC flag, 2) re-export model metadata and assert head counts, 3) run int8 quant (no group) to see if drift persists, 4) run canonical conversion with `--preserve-layout`.
sofia: doing 1&2 now. tokenizer: original vocab.json has `normalize_form: "NFKC"` and merges.json contains special-case zero-width joiner rules. our shim had `normalize_form: "NFKC"` but our loader applies NFC -> mismatch.
anita: loader bug then. that explains per-token misalignment. for rotary: i pushed a small patch to conversion to prefer explicit `head_dim` over inferred packing if both present. tentative PR #1029.
sofia: quick bench after disabling our loader normalization (match upstream):
```
zeta baseline (fp16): p95 latency 78ms, avg top1 0.62
zeta int4 (reconv, preserve-layout): p95 61ms, avg top1 0.60
```
sofia: much closer. so NV: major problem was tokenizer normalization (index shift) + conversion headpacking inference. both compound to cause embedding drift.
liam: nice catch. for completeness we should run the standard eval suite (long-answer + summarization) and compare ROUGE/BLEU. also add a unit test: roundtrip tokenization idempotence for common prefixes.
kevin: I'll run the eval overnight and check regression alerts in Optimize. if numbers hold we'll merge PR and re-run canary on Dedicated.
sofia: TL;DR: don't assume normalization semantics; prefer explicit metadata for head counts/head_dim in conversion; add tokenization idempotence check to onboarding flow.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: zeta13b-int4-reconv -> dedicated-pool-3 at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z. :rocket:
sofia: tagging @anita @kevin for followups. I'll file a short onboarding checklist entry and update the conversion README.
anita: adding a small script to validate rotary scale uniformity across heads. will attach in PR.
kevin: thanks all. followups tomorrow.
